title: The Faithful Clock
premise: In 1899 London, Mirabel Ravensworth works as driver and errand-runner for suffragist Adeline Hartwell, secretly reading the letters she carries and nursing a quiet love for clockmaker Elias Thorne, whose workshop faces demolition by the railway trust. When a census taker's probing questions expose that Mirabel is living under a name that isn't legally hers—the daughter of a hanged forger—she becomes vulnerable to blackmail by the trust's agent, who wants her to betray Adeline's campaign. Torn between duty to the woman who saved her, love for Elias, and the threat of ruin, Mirabel races to help finish the great astronomical clock Elias has promised to the Guild before the workshop falls and the century turns. She ultimately refuses the blackmail at terrible personal cost, testifies truthfully at the inquiry, and finds that honesty—not invisibility—is what secures her place: the workshop survives through public outcry, Adeline claims her as family, and she and Elias begin the new century together beneath the finished clock.
about_author: Xanthe Eriksen is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing Victorian trade ledgers and census schedules in northern England before turning to fiction full-time. She writes historical novels about working women whose names history nearly forgot.

chapters.title: The Weight of Other People's Words
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Establishes her double life: driving Adeline Hartwell through fog-bound London while quietly steaming open letters in the carriage. We learn she reads everything but keeps nothing. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Twelve Bells on Fetter Lane
chapters.summary: Mirabel delivers a summons to Elias Thorne's clock workshop and lingers too long among the gears. Their wary flirtation begins; he notices she can read a schematic. POV alternates briefly to Elias. Beat: longing she refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Census Man's Question
chapters.summary: A census taker visits Adeline's house and asks Mirabel for her legal name and parentage. Her evasive answers plant a seed of suspicion—and reach the ears of Mr. Calloway, the railway trust's agent. Beat: the first crack in her invisibility.

chapters.title: What Her Father Left
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Mirabel's childhood as daughter of a master forger hanged at Newgate, and how Adeline took her in under a new name. Present-day Mirabel burns her last false papers. Beat: grief braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: The Clock That Must Outlive Us
chapters.summary: Elias reveals his commission: an astronomical clock for the Guild, due when the century turns—but the trust's compulsory purchase order will raze the workshop first. He asks Mirabel, half-joking, to steal him time. Beat: shared defiance.

chapters.title: Letters Worth Stealing
chapters.summary: Mirabel intercepts correspondence showing the trust bribing officials to fast-track the demolition. She must decide whether to pass it to Adeline and reveal she reads the mail. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Confession by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Mirabel confesses to Adeline that she reads every letter. Instead of anger, Adeline makes her official reader—a role of real trust. Beat: the fragile warmth of being seen.

chapters.title: Calloway's Offer
chapters.summary: Calloway corners Mirabel: he knows her father's name and her forged identity. Deliver Adeline's campaign plans, or be exposed and transported like him. Beat: cold fear; the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Half a Movement
chapters.summary: Adeline's suffragist allies plan a public demonstration at the Guild exhibition. Mirabel feeds Calloway harmless truths to buy time, hating herself. Beat: the corrosive arithmetic of small betrayals.

chapters.title: Gears in the Dark
chapters.summary: Mirabel helps Elias work nights on the clock as the eviction date nears. A tender scene between them is interrupted by news that the trust has moved the deadline up. Beat: love against the clock, literally.

chapters.title: The Sisterhood of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Adeline's network rallies: printers, laundresses, and clerks offer shelter and witnesses. Mirabel realizes she has a community worth protecting. Beat: belonging as both comfort and stakes-raiser.

chapters.title: A Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Calloway escalates, showing Mirabel a copy of the census page with her father's name inked beside hers. He gives her one week. Beat: dread closing in; the noose of paperwork.

chapters.title: What Adeline Would Do
chapters.summary: Mirabel debates fleeing to France with money stolen from the campaign fund—her darkest hour. She almost does it. Beat: self-loathing and temptation held in perfect balance.

chapters.title: The Escapement
chapters.summary: Elias teaches Mirabel the escapement mechanism—the part that lets a clock release time in measured beats. The metaphor lands: survival is not hiding but choosing your moments. Beat: quiet epiphany.

chapters.title: Betrayal, Almost
chapters.summary: Under pressure, Mirabel hands Calloway a document—but it's a forgery of her own making, planted to discredit him. Her father's craft, turned honest. Beat: inheritance reclaimed as weapon.

chapters.title: The Raid on Fetter Lane
chapters.summary: Trust men raid the workshop early; Elias is injured defending the clock's core movement. Mirabel drives him to safety through the city, pursued. Beat: terror, then fierce clarity—she cannot hide anymore.

chapters.title: Everything on the Record
chapters.summary: At the public inquiry into the compulsory purchase, Mirabel takes the stand, admits her true identity, and exposes Calloway's forged evidence and bribes. Beat: climax—ruin risked for truth.

chapters.title: The Verdict of Strangers
chapters.summary: The inquiry suspends the demolition pending investigation; Calloway is discredited and flees. But Mirabel's confession costs her Adeline's household position—for form's sake, at least. Beat: victory shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Hands on the Dial
chapters.summary: Mirabel returns to the workshop not as a visitor but as Elias's apprentice. Together they assemble the final train of wheels as the year runs out. Beat: joy earned through wreckage.

chapters.title: Adeline's Letter
chapters.summary: Adeline writes Mirabel a letter—one she doesn't need to steam open—formally naming her heir to her estate and family. Beat: inheritance redefined; tears finally allowed.

chapters.title: Midnight, December 31st
chapters.summary: The astronomical clock strikes the century in before a crowd at the Guild; the workshop stands, the campaign marches past its windows. Elias and Mirabel watch the figures turn. Beat: triumph, tenderness, the future arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: The Faithful Clock
chapters.summary: Epilogue, spring 1901. Mirabel signs her own name—Ravensworth, chosen and true—to her apprenticeship papers. Closing meditation: a faithful clock does not hide its ticking. Beat: peace; a life fully owned.
